text:
helen: FYI vendor AuroraML Pty Ltd (AU) sent invoice and charged 10% GST. They also asked Redwood to gross-up for an alleged "withholding levy" applied by our bank when sending AUD. Invoice link: https://vendors.example.com/auroraml/invoice/AM-2026-888

sam: Paste the invoice lines and ABN please? Australia GST is 10% so amounts will look familiar but need to confirm ABN.

helen: Invoice snippet: 
```
Vendor: AuroraML Pty Ltd
ABN: 12 345 678 901
Invoice#: AM-2026-888
Service: Managed inference cluster (month of Jun)
Amount ex GST: 18,000.00 AUD
GST 10%: 1,800.00 AUD
Total: 19,800.00 AUD
```
They attached a bank SWIFT showing a 2.5% deduction labelled "tax withheld" and asked us to gross-up or send gross payment to cover the shortfall.

tax-ops: Quick check: ABN 12 345 678 901 returned NO MATCH on ABN Lookup. That is a red flag. For B2B supplies to an Australian-registered business, supplier should provide valid ABN and generally shouldn't charge GST to a foreign buyer if place of supply rules say services supplied to an overseas recipient are GST-free. If supplier is registered, they must remit GST. But if ABN doesn't validate, we need proof of registration.

sam: Also: which Redwood entity is the bill-to on the PO? If it's Redwood Australia Pty Ltd (we have one for local ops) we'd expect GST to apply; if it's Redwood EU, they shouldn't charge GST. AP has the PO showing Redwood EU Services GmbH.

ap-bot: (automated) PO metadata: Bill-to: Redwood EU Services GmbH (EU VAT: EU123456789). Vendor onboarding: ABN provided but not validated. Vendor flag: requested_gross_up:true.

helen: Vendor replied saying their ABN is new and their ABN lookup is showing latency; they claim the SWIFT deduction is a government tax in the correspondent country and ask Redwood to gross-up. They included a screenshot of a bank advice showing a 2.5% deduction labelled "TAX".

tax-ops: From tax standpoint: banks/treasury deductions are not the vendor's tax obligation in most cases. If the vendor claims the deduction is an official tax, ask for the taxing authority name and an official certificate of withholding. Without that, we should not gross-up. Also require vendor to prove ABN via ACN/ASIC extract or an ABN confirmation from the Australian Business Register (ABR).

legal: Agree. Ask for (1) ABR confirmation or ASIC company extract matching AuroraML Pty Ltd and the ABN, (2) corrected invoice if the supply is to Redwood EU (showing net/gst-free or reverse-charge equivalent), (3) if they insist the deduction is a government tax, a formal certificate of tax withheld showing authority stamp and instructions for reclaim. If they can't provide, we will not gross-up.

sam: AP ops: we can pay the invoiced total if vendor is validated. If ABN remains unverified, AP will pay the net (excluding GST) and hold the GST line in suspense pending vendor docs. We will also not gross-up for alleged bank charges. For recurring payments, insist on clean docs for the next period.

helen: Draft reply I'll send: "Hi AuroraML Please provide proof of ABN via ABR lookup or ASIC company extract, and confirm the billed legal entity. If this supply is to Redwood EU Services GmbH (we provided EU VAT ID on PO), please reissue the invoice net of Australian GST with a note 'supply to non-resident buyer - GST not applicable' or provide evidence of ABN validation if you're GST-registered. We do not gross-up for intermediary bank charges or unsubstantiated 'tax' deductions. If this is a contractual requirement, please point to the clause and provide a signed amendment." I'll CC @tax-ops and @legal.

tax-ops: Add: if they provide an official certificate of tax withheld from an authority, we'll evaluate reclaim procedures, but gross-up remains a last resort and requires legal sign-off. Also confirm beneficiary bank account name matches vendor legal name to avoid routing/fraud.

legal: If vendor threatens to withhold services, escalate to vendor management/sales. We can offer to pay net now and clear GST after validation. Do not accept indemnities that are open-ended.

ap-bot: (automated) AP action: place vendor on verification hold for GST line. Do not release GST to vendor until ABN validated or corrected invoice provided.

helen: Sending the reply now. Will update thread when they respond. Closing for now unless vendor pushes. :thumbsup:
